 Ex-Netanyahu Aide Behind Election Day Tip That Led to Arab Activists' Arrests, Report Says
 Netanyahu's chief of staff referred Israeli police to a source who claimed to have information about three United Arab List activists, leading to their arrest on Election Day. The source was a former employee of the PM's office

Credit: Oren Ben Hakoon Noa Shpigel Follow 09:23 PM • November 15 2026 IST A former employee at the office of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was the figure who passed what he claimed were allegations to the police that three Arab Israeli activists were involved in election fraud, Israel's Channel 12 News reported on Sunday. 
 Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, contacted Israel Police Commissioner Danny Levy and said the United Arab List activists allegedly intended to pay voters to support the party the day before the Knesset election, Channel 12 said. Norden referred police to a source who allegedly possessed information about the three activists to back the claim, the report added. That source was the former Netanyahu bureau employee. 
 That same source had worked until recently at the Prime Minister's Office and was considered close to Yossi Shelley, who served as the bureau's director general. 
 Close Ido Norden speaking at the Knesset last year. Credit: Sraya Diamant Ido Norden speaking at the Knesset last year. Credit: Sraya Diamant The police arrested the activists on Election Day following the tip-off. Moreover, Shin Bet security service chief David Zini asked Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to wiretap five Arab MKs as part of the suspicion of foreign involvement in the elections. The attorney general rejected the request, the report said. 
 Moreover, Zini also told Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot at a meeting a few days after the election that "There has been intelligence here since 2018 that Arabs are stealing elections in Israel. All the [former] Shin Bet chiefs ignored it."
 The Prime Minister's Office denied the report, saying it is part of "grave attempts to suppress the election-tampering affair."
 In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said Chief of Staff Ido Norden contacted the police about the allegations but denied any additional involvement, calling the claims defamatory lies. "He never spoke with police intelligence officials or anyone else involved in the investigation," it said. 
 Close Shin Bet chief David Zini and Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara last month. Credit: Olivier Fitoussi Shin Bet chief David Zini and Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara last month. Credit: Olivier Fitoussi The report on the wiretapping request follows Zini's request to question under caution former Joint List leader Ayman Odeh, Joint List MK Ahmad Tibi and United Arab List chairman Mansour Abbas, despite a lack of evidence against them. 
 Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot said in response that the conduct of Netanyahu and the people around him "poses a tangible, direct and immediate threat to Israeli democracy." He said that "under no circumstances should Netanyahu remain at the helm of government for even one more minute." 
 Eisenkot further added that "it is clear that as long as he remains in office, Israel will no longer have free and fair elections. This is the central consideration guiding me in every coalition negotiation I am conducting these days."

 Eisenkot called for an immediate investigation into allegations, demanded answers from police and the Shin Bet and pledged to seek a commission of inquiry into the conduct of the prime minister's office and security agencies before and on Election Day.
 Following the report, the Joint List issued a statement calling for the attorney general to open a criminal investigation "into Netanyahu, his chief of staff and everyone involved in framing the case" in what the party called "an attempt to steal the election" by the prime minister.
 Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen said the report "raises serious suspicions that Netanyahu attempted a coup by criminally using the police against the Arab public and its leaders."
 "The report that the Shin Bet security service was asked to wiretap Arab lawmakers makes the allegations even more serious. This is conduct characteristic of repressive regimes," Jabareen added, calling on Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to investigate the matter.
